 S/o H. Rumvunga (L)
 R/o Lawngtlai AOC Advocate for the Petitioner : Mrs. Mary Lalruatkimi Khiangte Advocate for the Respondent :
 BEFORE  HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE RAJESH MAZUMDAR  ORDER 07.04.2026 Heard Ms. Savita Sarna, learned counsel appearing for the applicant in I.A. (Civil) No.
135/2025.
By referring to the earlier orders of this Court passed in the I.A., the learned counsel has submitted that the matter would require a consideration Page No.# 2/3 today and a disposal.
It is seen that the private respondents have filed their objections to the I.A.

During the course of deliberation, a consensus has been arrived at by the counsel for the parties that the entire writ petition can be taken up for disposal on a convenient date, preparing an end to the litigation itself.
Accordingly, this Court also deems it fit to direct this matter to be listed on 28.04.2026, on which day an attempt would be made to dispose the writ petition.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the applicant in the I.A, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) has submitted that it would be reflected from the contents of the I.A itself that the guidelines laid down by the JICA require the relevant law of the land to be followed and the guidelines do not act as supreme over the local, State or Central laws of the concerned government.

She has also submitted that the JICA is not involved either in computing, evaluating or disbursing compensation with regard to acquisition of immovable property made or carrying out projects proposed by the authorities.
She has also prayed for the liberty to be allowed to appear through VC on 28.04.2026, in the event it is not possible for her to attend the court physically.
Page No.# 3/3 Allowing the liberty, list this matter again on 28.04.2026, on which day an attempt would be made to dispose the writ petition on merits.
